title: What the equals sign really means
examples: What does the equals sign mean?
How do I find a missing number?

left.ask: What does the equals sign mean?

explain.say: Is the equals sign just a signal that the answer comes next? Not quite! Look at the seesaw: 3 plus 4 on the left and 7 on the right. It is level. Equals means both sides are worth the same.

draw.text: What the equals sign really means

left.ask: What does the equals sign mean?

explain.say: So you can flip it round: 7 equals 3 plus 4. Look, the seesaw is still level! The answer does not have to come last. Does that surprise you?
Both sides can be sums: 5 plus 2 equals 6 plus 1, because both sides make 7. See the level beam? Can you find another pair that makes 7?
Here is a puzzle: 4 plus what equals 8? To keep the seesaw level, the left side must make 8 too. 4 and 4 make 8, so the missing number is 4. Can you see why?

left.ask: How do I find a missing number?

explain.say: Brilliant! Now 6 plus 3 against 10. The 10 side drops, so they are not equal: 6 plus 3 is 9, not 10. Wow: Robert Recorde invented the equals sign in 1557, using two lines of the same length! Try this: 10 equals 7 plus what?

faq.q: What does the equals sign mean?
faq.a: It means the two sides are worth exactly the same, like a level seesaw. 3 plus 4 equals 7 because both sides are 7.
Yes. 7 equals 3 plus 4 is just as true as 3 plus 4 equals 7. The equals sign only says that both sides match.

faq.q: How do I find a missing number?
faq.a: Work out what the full side makes, then ask what is needed to match it. For 4 plus what equals 8, the left side must make 8, so the missing number is 4.
Yes. 5 plus 2 equals 6 plus 1, because both sides make 7. The equals sign compares the two totals.
asks: Can there be a sum on both sides?

faq.a: Robert Recorde, a Welsh mathematician, in 1557. He drew two parallel lines of the same length, because he felt nothing could be more equal.
asks: Where does the equals sign come from?

facts: The equals sign means both sides have the same value.
Robert Recorde introduced the equals sign in 1557 in his book The Whetstone of Witte.

quiz.why: 5 plus 3 is 8, so both sides match.
6 plus 4 makes 10, so the missing number is 4.
